prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, which opened moire quantum matter.

statement.case_for: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model is exactly the kind of result I trust: a simple model whose single control parameter, the twist angle, produces a surprising and universal consequence (nearly flat bands at a magic angle), and which was then tested directly. The 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity gave the prediction decisive experimental confirmation, and within about eight years independent groups reproduced and extended it across graphene multilayers and TMD moire systems. Five of eight members placed it in their top three, and it is the one shortlisted candidate with that breadth of support from both theory and experimental members. It is a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration with a mechanism that is understood, not only a platform that works. I ranked B008 first on conceptual grounds, but after reading the ballots I see no path for it that does not rest on two quite different discoveries bridged by a common theme, and only two members ranked it at all.
statement.case_against: The field is young, and the origin of the superconductivity is still contested, so we would be rewarding a platform before its central physical question is settled. Priority is also not clean: earlier band-structure work on twisted graphene layers (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell and colleagues) anticipated parts of the picture, and the first author of the experimental papers (Yuan Cao) and contemporaneous groups are outside the three-name limit. If the committee thinks the pairing mechanism must be understood before a prize, B013 is early and B008 or B061 are safer.

responses.point: Olsson ranks B013 first as the clean discovery of a tunable platform with reproducible correlated and superconducting signatures, while noting the junior first author and earlier related theory should be checked against the historical record.
responses.response: I agree with her on the strength of the experimental signature and with her caution on priority. The earlier continuum-band work on twisted layers did not identify a single magic angle at which the bands become flat, nor predict that interactions would then dominate, and that is the Bistritzer-MacDonald contribution. So I think the attribution is defensible for MacDonald and Bistritzer. The omission of Cao is a real cost that the three-person limit forces, and I would not hide it in the citation.

responses.point: Danielsson values prediction followed by experimental confirmation but asks whether recognition is premature given that the superconducting pairing mechanism is still debated and the field is under a decade old.
responses.response: I take the maturity point seriously and it is the strongest argument against my own preference. My answer is that the discovery, namely flat bands whose filling controls correlated phases, is reproduced and its interpretation is stable, whereas the pairing mechanism is a downstream question; I would not make a prize wait for it. I do not accept his first-place B009 as a clear alternative on maturity grounds: it is also a large-collaboration result with a contested split of credit between instigators and analysts.

responses.point: Eriksson puts B019 first as mature, conceptually clean topological theory with a decisive HgTe experiment, and B013 second, noting that it is slightly early.
responses.response: We largely agree on the pair. B019 is more mature, and I ranked it third, but its attribution is the more damaged one: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe realisation that Molenkamp measured, and the 3D work by Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, and the ARPES groups is intertwined with it. A three-name list drawn from Kane, Mele and Molenkamp leaves out the prediction that the experiment tested. B013's credited trio matches the prediction and the experiment better, and I would rather accept some immaturity than a more doubtful attribution.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B061 first and B008 third, arguing that B008 is long mature and urgent given the ages of the principals, though it is two discoveries bridged by a theme.
responses.response: I agree that B008 is urgent and mature, and it remains my conceptual favourite, so I keep it as an alternative. Where I part from her is on a joint citation: Bohm is deceased, so the Aharonov-Bohm part rests on one living name for a 1959 paper written with a deceased co-author, and the committee would have to word it carefully. On B061, I rank it lower than she does mainly because the redefinition of the second is pending and the technology is still advancing, but I accept that it is sharply defined, reproduced by several national laboratories, and a stronger alternative than most of the field.

responses.point: Johansson ranks B018 first and B034 second, defending Cirac and Zoller as a compact theory pair whose proposals defined two experimental programmes, and says B013 lies outside his core expertise.
responses.response: I agree that Cirac and Zoller are a clean pair, and B034 is a serious candidate, but I think it fits less well as a prize for physical discovery: its decisive experimental realisations came from others and were partly honoured in 2012, so it risks a prize for a blueprint. For B018 I share his worry that the credited trio omits Andreas Wallraff, who was central to the first strong-coupling experiment, which makes the allocation harder than for B013.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a prize for B013 before the superconducting pairing mechanism is understood.
How much weight the omission of Yuan Cao and the earlier twisted-graphene band-structure work should carry against the credited trio; I cannot check priority independently from the provided files.
Whether a two-part prize pairing B008 with another achievement is feasible within the three-person limit, since B008 would consume two names and B013 three.
Whether B061 would be preferred on maturity grounds by the members who ranked it first, and how the redefinition of the second should affect timing.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. I note that Goran Johansson and Eva Olsson are in the neighbouring Gothenburg physics environment at Chalmers, and the GU and Chalmers departments are closely linked, but I have no collaboration with them or with any credited candidate.
